name: Illinois
summary: Illinois BTM C&I storage value is concentrated on the ComEd (PJM) side. Capacity PLC reduction is worth about $122/kW-yr for summer-2026 peaks (2027/28 BRA $333.44/MW-day at the cap) and $118.63 for 2028/29. Network transmission (NSPL) adds about $46/kW-yr. ComEd's Distribution Facilities Charge ($13-15/kW-month in 2025, billed on the 9am-6pm weekday 30-minute max) makes daytime demand shaving valuable but needs long duration. Ameren (MISO Zone 4) capacity is far weaker and volatile (2026/27 annualized $126.19/MW-day, about $46/kW-yr). DS-3 delivery ($9.69/kW secondary in 2026) moves to on-peak kVA billing in January 2027. CRGA (signed 2026-01-08) keeps a $250-300/kWh DG storage rebate (standalone eligible, max 5 kWh/kW, 25 MWh cap). Since June 2026 the rebate requires 5 summers in the utility Rider SDVPP (weekday 4-6 pm, about $10/kW-season, launching 2027), and that program's export-capability requirement may clash with non-export designs. Key risks: PLC/NSPL savings only reach RES customers with pass-through contracts; PLC savings and PJM DR overlap on the same kW; Chicago Loop networks cap expedited interconnection at 50 kW; and indoor Li-ion fire-area limits (about 600 kWh) apply in Chicago and IFC jurisdictions.
default_energy_price_note: Approximate all-in commercial $/kWh (analyst assumption, used only to cost round-trip losses). Enter the site’s actual price.
data_notes: Researched 2026-10-01 by the expert panel from web-search summaries of primary sources (direct document retrieval was blocked in the research environment). Treat medium/low-confidence values as screening estimates.

utilities.name: Commonwealth Edison Company (ComEd)
utilities.default_supply_notes: Customers of 100 kW and above (supply competitively declared) default to Rate BESH: hourly energy at PJM ComEd-zone prices, plus a Capacity Charge = Capacity Obligation (PLC) x Capacity Charge Rate ($/kW-month, reset each June), plus transmission and ancillary charges. Customers under 100 kW can take fixed-price BES. Most large C&I buy from a RES. The 100 kW threshold is expert knowledge; the tariff text was not re-verified in this session.
utilities.network_grid_notes: ComEd serves the Chicago Loop and other dense downtown areas through underground secondary voltage networks (area/spot networks) fed by multiple primary circuits. Under Part 466, non-exporting DER on an area network gets Level 3 review only if nameplate is 50 kW or less, inverter-based, non-export controlled, and aggregate network generation is at most the lower of 5% of network max load or 50 kVA. Larger systems go to Level 4 study. Expect network-protector coordination, minimum-import requirements and long studies for C&I BESS in the Loop.

interconnection.rule_name: 83 Ill. Adm. Code 466 (DER Interconnection Standards, <=10 MVA); Part 467 for >10 MVA. ComEd DER Interconnection Requirements (Rev. 2026-09-10).

tracks.name: Level 1
tracks.conditions: Export capacity <=25 kW and nameplate <=50 kW (if export not limited, nameplate <=25 kW); lab-certified equipment.

tracks.name: Level 2
tracks.conditions: Lab-certified inverter-based, nameplate limit by line voltage at POI: <5 kV <=500 kW; 5-<15 kV <=3 MW; 15-<30 kV <=4 MW; 30-69 kV <=5 MW. Screens apply.

tracks.name: Level 3
tracks.conditions: Non-exporting DER. For area networks: nameplate <=50 kW, lab-certified inverter, acceptable non-export controls, aggregate network DER <= lower of 5% of network max load or 50 kVA. Limit for radial non-export Level 3 not verified.

tracks.name: Level 4
tracks.conditions: Nameplate <=10 MVA that does not qualify for (or failed) Levels 1-3; full study.

interconnection.non_export_path: Part 466 distinguishes export capacity from nameplate (e.g., Level 1 allows 50 kW nameplate with <=25 kW export), and Level 3 is the non-export path. On ComEd 12 kV-class radial feeders most C&I BESS (<=3 MW inverter-based) fit Level 2 screens. ComEd requires customer DER transformers to be Delta on the ComEd (high) side. ComEd is developing flexible interconnection (Docket 24-0181).
interconnection.storage_specific_notes: Important: CRGA-era DG storage rebates require the system to be capable of supplying energy to the grid and to join the SDVPP (dispatch Jun-Sep weekdays 4-6 pm). A strictly non-exporting Level 3 design may conflict with rebate/SDVPP measurement. Verify Rider SDVPP metering before choosing non-export. Timelines and Level 2 screen details were not verified.

tariffs.name: Rate RDS - Small Load Delivery Class (0-100 kW)

applicability.text: Nonresidential retail delivery under Rate RDS; delivery class based on maximum demand (0-100 kW). Delivery charges apply regardless of supplier (BESH/BES or RES).

demand_charges.label: Distribution Facilities Charge (DFC), secondary voltage
demand_charges.hours: 9:00 AM-6:00 PM Mon-Fri, excluding certain holidays (Maximum Kilowatts Delivered = highest 30-minute demand in that window during the billing month)
demand_charges.notes: Value shown is for the January 2025 billing period (latest confirmed). The 2026 DFC (effective Jan 2026 under the multi-year rate plan) was not verified and is likely higher. Load outside 9am-6pm weekdays does not set the DFC, so off-peak and weekend charging is free from a delivery-demand standpoint. Customers under 100 kW usually take fixed-price BES supply or RES supply.

energy_rates.label: Supply energy (BESH hourly default or RES contract)
energy_rates.hours: hourly (BESH tracks PJM ComEd-zone hourly prices)

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: ComEd Capacity PLC: average of the customer's metered demand in the 5 summer hours of highest PJM RTO load (PJM 5CP) and the 5 summer hours of highest ComEd zone load (ComEd 5CP), i.e. up to 10 hours per summer (Jun-Sep). It is then adjusted by PJM factors and applies from the following June 1 for 12 months.
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: 1 kW of capacity PLC reduction ~= BRA price x days in delivery year / 1000 (scaling factors assumed 1.0). 2025/26: $269.92/MW-day x 365 / 1000 = $98.52/kW-yr; 2026/27: $329.17 x 365 / 1000 = $120.15/kW-yr; 2027/28: $333.44 x 366 (Feb-2028 leap) / 1000 = $122.04/kW-yr; 2028/29: $325.00 x 365 / 1000 = $118.63/kW-yr. Timing: summer-2026 coincident-peak performance sets the PLC billed Jun-2027 to May-2028, so a battery operating in summer 2026 earns the 2027/28 value ($122.04/kW-yr); summer 2027 earns 2028/29 ($118.63). Actual billed value = PLC x Final Zonal RPM Scaling Factor x Forecast Pool Requirement x Final Zonal Net Load Price; those factors (and ComEd's loss/weather adjustments to the PLC) were NOT verified in this session, so treat +/-10% as the uncertainty band. Monthly equivalent ~$10.17/kW-month for 2027/28.
coincident_peak_charges.passthrough_notes: BESH (ComEd hourly default supply) customers pay the Capacity Charge = Capacity Obligation x Capacity Charge Rate ($/kW-month, reset each June), so PLC savings flow through directly. RES (retail supplier) customers realize the savings only if the contract passes capacity through at the customer's actual PLC (index/pass-through). Fixed all-in contracts embed the PLC at signing, so savings appear only at renewal. Small-load customers on fixed-price BES do not see PLC savings because capacity is embedded in the $/kWh rate.

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: Network Service PLC (NSPL) is a separate value that ComEd assigns to each account. ComEd's exact NSPL method (typically the customer's load at the zonal annual peak hour of the prior calendar year) was NOT verified in this session.
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: ComEd zone NITS rate effective 2025-06-01 = $46,025/MW-yr (ATRR $992,308,573), so 1 kW of NSPL reduction ~= $46.03/kW-yr of network transmission. Excludes Schedule 12 RTEP/TEC and other NSPL-allocated charges, which would add to it. The rate for June 2026 onward was not verified. Earlier values: $34,401 (Jun-2018) and $37,749 (Jun-2021), so the rate has risen about 22% since 2021.
coincident_peak_charges.passthrough_notes: Transmission (NITS) is charged by PJM to the LSE based on NSPL. Savings are realized under BESH/ComEd transmission charges, or under a RES contract only if transmission is a pass-through line item.

tariffs.storage_notes: No DFC ratchet was identified, but this is unverified. Note that delivery-class assignment is driven by the customer's peak demand: shaving the peak below a class boundary changes the class, and the 2025 DFC $/kW does not decline monotonically by class (Small $14.58 > Medium $13.24). One battery dispatch window of about 2-4 pm to 6 pm CPT on hot weekdays can stack the DFC (9am-6pm max), PLC (5+5 CP hours) and the CRGA SDVPP (4-6 pm Jun-Sep weekdays). However, the DFC requires all-weekday 9-hour coverage of the monthly max, so long-duration products (3-5 h) are favored.

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: MISO capacity obligation assigned by Ameren Illinois to each account. Ameren's PLC derivation method (which peak hours, seasonal or annual) was NOT verified in this session.
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: MISO PRA 2026/27 Zone 4 (Zones 1-7) cleared Summer $424.30, Fall $33.92, Winter $35.97 and Spring $7.61 per MW-day. Day-weighted average = (424.30x92 + 33.92x91 + 35.97x90 + 7.61x92)/365 = $126.19/MW-day, matching MISO/Modo's published annualized value. $126.19 x 365 / 1000 = $46.06/kW-yr if the tag is a single annual PLC. 85% of the value is summer: $424.30 x 92 / 1000 = $39.04/kW per summer season. 2025/26 for comparison: summer $666.50 (record), annualized about $217.6/MW-day (implied by the 42% decrease to $126.19), or about $79/kW-yr.

panel_notes.note: The ComEd DFC bills the highest 30-minute demand between 9am and 6pm on weekdays, so a battery must cover the whole 9-hour window, not just the afternoon. Peak shaving across a delivery-class boundary changes the DFC $/kW, and Small Load's 2025 rate ($14.58) is higher than Medium's ($13.24). Model the class reassignment.

panel_notes.topic: Rebate now comes with a 5-year VPP obligation
panel_notes.note: Since June 1, 2026, taking the DG storage rebate commits the system to Rider SDVPP for 5 summers of weekday 4-6 pm dispatch at about $10/kW-season. Check that the dispatch counts export, and that a non-export interconnection doesn't void eligibility, before booking the $250-300/kWh.

DS-3 moves to kVA billing in January 2027, billed on the greater of on-peak apparent demand or 50% of off-peak apparent demand. Batteries that charge hard overnight can set the bill, and poor power factor now costs money. Use the inverter's reactive capability and cap off-peak charging.

panel_notes.topic: MISO capacity is summer-weighted and volatile
panel_notes.note: Zone 4 capacity fell from a $666.50 summer clear (2025/26) to $424.30 (2026/27). About 85% of annual value is the summer season, so Ameren-side capacity savings are worth roughly $39-61/kW per summer, far less than PJM's ~$120/kW-yr on the ComEd side.

Most ComEd C&I load is on RES contracts. PLC and NSPL savings, worth about $122/kW-yr and $46/kW-yr, reach the customer only with a capacity/transmission pass-through product or at renewal. Fixed all-in deals lock in last year's tag. Put the contract structure in the site screen.

panel_notes.topic: PLC vs PJM DR double counting
panel_notes.note: In ComEd, DR nominations are measured against the PLC. Shaving the 10 PLC hours already captures the capacity value, and the same kW can't also be sold as Capacity Performance DR. Pick the higher-value path per site; DR helps when 5CP prediction is poor or the site is on a fixed-price contract.

PJM's 2028/29 simulation showed the ComEd LDA would have cleared at $776.69/MW-day without the $325 cap. If the cap/collar lapses, ComEd PLC value could more than double, which is upside for long-tenor PLC-based savings.

On ComEd's area/spot networks, Part 466 expedited (Level 3) review stops at 50 kW non-export with a 50 kVA network aggregate. Any 200 kW unit goes to a Level 4 study with network-protector and minimum-import constraints. Screen Loop sites out or assume long timelines.

Chicago's 2018 IFC-based code and most IL municipalities limit indoor Li-ion to about 600 kWh per fire area and need full plan review above 20 kWh. Multi-unit 200 kW/600 kWh stacks usually go outdoor or into dedicated rated rooms with sprinklers.

Covering the ComEd 9am-6pm DFC window, up to 10 PLC hours and the 4-6 pm SDVPP needs long duration. The 2.1 h 200 kW/418 kWh unit typically protects only an afternoon slice, so derate its DFC value or pair it with 3-5 h units.

panel_notes.note: Parts of ComEd and Ameren still run 4 kV-class circuits, where Part 466 Level 2 caps inverter DER at 500 kW. Check the feeder voltage (hosting capacity map) before quoting multi-unit systems.
